interpretation: Receptors with established roles in extrinsic apoptosis. TNFRSF1A can also support survival and inflammatory signaling.
FADD and TRADD are adaptors; CASP8 and CASP10 are initiator caspases; BID links receptor signaling to mitochondrial apoptosis. These genes do not all encode adaptors.
Selected regulators with established cell-death inhibitory functions. Effects depend on stimulus, isoform and cellular context; an aggregate RNA score is not a resistance measurement.
Includes mitochondrial permeabilization factors, apoptosome components and an IAP antagonist. CASP9 is the initiator caspase in this set.
Selected executioner caspases. RNA abundance does not measure proteolytic activation.
Regulators associated with necroptotic signaling, with additional functions in other death and inflammatory pathways. RIPK1 is not required for every route to RIPK3 activation.

Descriptive two-gene set. MLKL is the terminal necroptotic effector; PGAM5 is a mitochondrial phosphatase and is not an established obligatory necroptotic executor. This score must not be presented as a canonical necroptosis-execution score.
Contains inflammasome sensors, the PYCARD adaptor and inflammatory caspases. Canonical and noncanonical pathways are represented in a combined set.
Selected gasdermins, not the complete family. Pore formation depends on cleavage and, for GSDMB, isoform composition.
Selected antigen-processing, peptide-loading and MHC-I regulatory genes. The set concerns TCR-mediated recognition and is not a direct measure of CD19 CAR recognition.
Combines NKG2D ligands with PVR and NECTIN2. PVR and NECTIN2 also engage inhibitory receptor systems and are not exclusively activating ligands.
Context-dependent immune interactions. HLA-E can engage inhibitory or activating NK receptors; CD47 also affects myeloid phagocytic responses.
